<RuleLanguageLinks current="javascript" languages={[{"id":"javascript","label":"JavaScript (and super languages)","href":"/linter/rules/use-simplified-boolean-return/javascript/"}]} />

:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.0`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/useSimplifiedBooleanReturn`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has a [**safe**](/linter/#safe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`unicorn/prefer-boolean-return`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/main/docs/rules/prefer-boolean-return.md)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useSimplifiedBooleanReturn": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Return conditions directly instead of using `if` statements that only return `true` or `false`.

An `if` statement whose branches only return `true` and `false` is a long way of
returning the condition itself. The same applies to an `if` statement that returns
`true` or `false`, followed directly by a `return` of the opposite value.
Returning the condition directly is shorter and easier to read.

When the condition doesn't always produce a boolean, the fix converts it with `!!`
so the function still returns `true` or `false`.

A sequence of early returns that all return the same value is not reported, because
rewriting only the last one would break up the group:

```js
function isEmpty(value) {
    if (value === null) {
        return true;
    }
    if (value === "") {
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}
```

## Examples

### Invalid

```js
function isPositive(value) {
    if (value > 0) {
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}
```

        return false;
    }

}

### Valid

```js
function isPositive(value) {
    return value > 0;
}

function hasItems(items) {
    return !!items.length;
}

function check(value) {
    if (value > 0) {
        return true;
    }
    log(value);
    return false;
}
```
